maintenanceGuides.title: Everyday Phone & Laptop Care
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Most hardware breakdowns happen from everyday physical stress and trapped heat. A few simple handling habits prevent premature screen cracks, hinge failures, and worn-out charging ports.
stepByStepGuidance: Use two hands to open your laptop from the center of the lid, not from the top corners, to avoid twisting the display hinges.
Keep your laptop on a flat desk or hard book. Soft blankets and pillows choke the cooling intake vents on the bottom, causing the processor to run hot.
Never yank charging cables out by the thin cord; always grasp the sturdy plastic plug head.
Invest in a durable protective case and tempered glass screen protector. A ₱750 protector absorbs shocks that would otherwise cost ₱8,000+ to repair.
whatToAvoid: Do not leave devices in closed vehicles during hot sunny days. Temperatures can easily reach 140°F (60°C), permanently damaging battery chemistry and warping adhesive seals.
Do not close laptop lids with pens, earbuds, or paper clips resting on the keyboard; this is the number one cause of shattered internal displays.
Do not eat crumbly food directly over keyboards. Crumbs jam scissor mechanisms and attract moisture.

maintenanceGuides.title: Battery Care: Keeping Your Battery Healthy
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Rechargeable batteries are like muscles: they wear out faster when stretched to extremes. Keeping your battery between 20% and 80% charge can easily double its useful lifespan.
stepByStepGuidance: Turn on 'Optimized Battery Charging' or 'Battery Protection' in your phone and laptop settings. This caps the charge at 80% to 85% when plugged in continuously.
Recharge your device when it reaches around 20% to 30% rather than waiting until it completely dies at 0%.
If you are putting an old phone or laptop in storage, charge it to about 50% first and turn it off completely. Storing a device at 0% can cause the battery to become chemically dead.
Keep your device cool while charging. Remove heavy, insulated phone cases if the phone feels noticeably warm while connected to a fast charger.
whatToAvoid: Do not use cheap, uncertified ₱100 sidewalk charging bricks. Cheap chargers deliver erratic electrical currents that degrade battery cells and pose fire risks.
Do not game or perform heavy video rendering while your phone is sitting under a blanket on a charger.
Do not panic if your battery runtime drops after 3 years. A battery replacement costs a tiny fraction of a new device and restores original battery life.

maintenanceGuides.title: Safe Cleaning: Screens, Keyboards & Ports
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Dust and grime do not just look untidy—they trap heat, insulate cooling fans, and clog charging ports. Here is how to safely clean electronics without stripping delicate screen coatings.
stepByStepGuidance: Power off and unplug your device before applying any cleaning cloth.
Use a clean, dry microfiber cloth (the type used for eyeglasses) to gently wipe fingerprints and smudges from glass screens.
If grime is stubborn, dampen the microfiber cloth with a small amount of 70% isopropyl alcohol or distilled water. Never spray liquid directly onto the screen or keyboard.
Use a wooden toothpick or dry, soft-bristle toothbrush to gently coax compacted pocket lint out of your phone's charging port.
Use short bursts of a compressed air can to blow out dust from laptop fan grilles and keyboard keys.
whatToAvoid: Never use household glass cleaner (like Windex), bleach, vinegar, or abrasive paper towels on screens. They strip the oleophobic anti-glare coatings.
Never poke metal paper clips, needles, or safety pins into charging ports. Metal can short-circuit the sensitive golden pin connectors.
Do not shake canned air upside down while spraying; this expels freezing liquid propellant that can crack delicate plastics.

maintenanceGuides.title: Storage Management: Freeing Up Drive Space
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Solid-state drives need breathing room to organize files and memory. When your drive is more than 90% full, everything slows to a crawl. Freeing up space restores responsiveness instantly.
stepByStepGuidance: Aim to keep at least 15% to 20% of your total storage drive free as temporary working room for the operating system.
Sort your phone photo library by videos; backing up or deleting large, forgotten 4K video clips immediately recovers gigabytes.
Review your downloaded podcast episodes, offline streaming playlists, and audiobooks.
Empty your operating system's 'Downloads' folder and clear out trash bins on external drives.
whatToAvoid: Do not install shady 'magic memory booster' or 'driver doctor' apps. They often install persistent background adware that slows your computer even further.
Do not ignore low storage warnings until your phone refuses to turn on. An overloaded operating system can fail to boot.

maintenanceGuides.title: Software Maintenance: Keeping It Smooth
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Over time, computers accumulate background startup programs, leftover caches, and forgotten browser extensions. Regular digital decluttering keeps your machine feeling snappy.
stepByStepGuidance: Restart your device at least once a week. Restarting flushes RAM memory leaks and completes pending system patches.
Check your 'Startup Apps' list in Windows or Mac settings and switch off apps (like Spotify, Discord, or game launchers) that try to launch automatically when you boot up.
Uninstall browser extensions you no longer use. Every active extension consumes memory on every tab you open.
Install regular security patches. Updates protect against modern vulnerabilities and fix system bugs.
whatToAvoid: Do not postpone critical security updates indefinitely.
Do not keep dozens of unused apps installed 'just in case'—you can always redownload them when needed.

maintenanceGuides.title: Repairing Instead of Immediately Replacing
maintenanceGuides.plainEnglishSummary: Most device frustrations stem from one worn-out component, not a failed processor. Identifying the specific failing part saves thousands of pesos.
stepByStepGuidance: If your phone battery drains in 2 hours: Replace the battery for ₱2,000–₱3,500 instead of spending ₱45,000+ on a new phone.
If your older laptop takes 5 minutes to boot up: The mechanical hard drive is likely the culprit. Swapping it for a ₱1,800 Solid State Drive (SSD) makes it boot in 15 seconds.
If a key fell off your keyboard: Individual keycaps and hinge clips cost ₱250 online and snap into place in seconds without replacing the whole laptop.
If your laptop fan is screaming constantly: A 20-minute thermal cleaning and new ₱450 thermal paste application cools the processor back to factory silence.
whatToAvoid: Do not assume that an out-of-warranty notice from a manufacturer means a device cannot be serviced. Independent repair shops and repair cafes service devices long after vendor support ends.
Do not discard a laptop simply because the charging cord broke. Replacement power adapters are widely available.

retirementThreshold.explanation: Screen replacement is a standardized, routine repair for almost all laptops and phones. It restores full visual quality for a fraction of a new machine's price.
retirementThreshold.recommendation: Obtain repair quotes from independent repair shops or local repair cafes.

retirementThreshold.issue: Worn Battery Lasting Less than 1 Hour
retirementThreshold.explanation: Batteries are consumable parts designed to be swapped every 3 to 4 years. Replacing a battery cell does not compromise the processor or memory.
retirementThreshold.recommendation: Order a certified replacement battery pack or have a technician install one.

retirementThreshold.issue: Severe Motherboard Water Corrosion & Short Circuits
retirementThreshold.explanation: When liquid penetrates internal multi-layer logic boards, microscopic copper traces dissolve and multiple microchips fail simultaneously. Diagnosis and micro-soldering often exceed the total value of the machine.
retirementThreshold.recommendation: Remove and sanitize the storage drive if salvageable, then route the chassis to a certified e-waste processor.

retirementThreshold.issue: Repair Estimate Exceeds 65% of Refurbished Replacement Cost
retirementThreshold.explanation: If multiple expensive components (e.g. cracked display + failed battery + dead motherboard) fail at once, purchasing a certified refurbished newer computer offers better longevity.
retirementThreshold.recommendation: Safely harvest reusable parts (RAM, SSD, power cord) and recycle the remaining carcass responsibly.

retirementThreshold.issue: Absence of Security Updates & Inability to Run Supported OS
retirementThreshold.explanation: Devices with 32-bit legacy processors that cannot receive modern TLS encryption security patches become vulnerable on the public internet.
retirementThreshold.recommendation: Repurpose as an offline typewriter, smart alarm, or media player; avoid using for online banking or email.
